_: The words this system's public API is allowed to use, and what each one means.
A shared prop name is a promise: `tone` must mean the same thing on every
component that has it, or an agent that learned it once learns it wrong
everywhere else. This file is the promise written down; scripts/lint-vocab.mjs
To add a value: put it here with its meaning. That is the whole cost, and it
is deliberately a sentence rather than a checkbox, because a value nobody can
describe in a sentence is a value that will drift.
`axis` names the ONE question a prop answers. A prop name that answers two
different questions is two props wearing one name.

values.warning: it needs attention but nothing is broken
values.danger: it is broken, failed, or over a limit
values.ai: produced by a model rather than a person

destructive.why: Apple HIG and Material both separate a destructive ACTION from a bad STATE, and so do we: a button says `destructive`, a badge or a bar says `danger`. Allowing both words on display components is how ProgressBar, Timeline and CountBadge each ended up with the action word for a status.

size.axis: how much room this thing takes

variant.axis: how much emphasis this CONTROL carries, and what role it plays

values.primary: the one action the screen wants
values.ghost: an action with no surface until hover
values.quiet: an action with no surface at all
values.filled: an action carrying a solid tone
values.dark: it sits on a dark surface
values.link: it navigates and looks like text

fill.axis: how a STATUS SURFACE is painted

values.soft: the tone's tint, for a quieter badge
values.plain: no surface, the tone as ink only

values.circle: a round box: a person's avatar, a round control
values.square: a rounded rectangle where a circle is the default: a team or an organisation rather than a person

placement.axis: where a SURFACE sits against the viewport

values.start: before the trigger in reading order (left in LTR, right in RTL)
values.end: after the trigger in reading order
values.side: beside the content, a fixed column (a card's horizontal media)
values.cover: behind the content, filling the surface (a card's media under its own text, scrim included)

surface.axis: what this thing is sitting ON, so it can stay visible against it
surface.why: Nine components answer this question and none of them was declared here, because the check only ever validated the words of props the file already knew. A control that dissolves into the surface behind it is the exact failure this axis exists to prevent, and it was the most-shared word in the system with nothing written down about it.

values.base: the default surface — a card or the page body. Form controls draw their resting border here
values.muted: the tinted surface (--muted): a page background, a PageHeader. A control drops its resting border and lets its white fill do the separating
values.card: inside a card, on white: an icon badge goes grey so it reads
values.page: on the grey page body: the same badge inverts to white

surface.note: Form controls answer `base` or `muted`; a block that sizes itself to a surface answers `card` or `page`. One axis, two grains of answer — a component takes the subset that makes sense for it, the way it does for `tone`.

as.axis: which HTML element this renders as, when the choice is the document's and not the component's
as.why: A heading level is a property of the page, not of the component: the same EmptyState is the page's h1 on an empty route and an h2 inside a card. Declaring the words keeps that a document decision and stops `as` drifting into a styling prop.

values.h1: this heading names the page. Only where nothing else does

appearance.axis: which of this component's OWN looks, when the choice is local and not a system-wide scale
appearance.why: Tabs are underline or pills; a meta line is meta or eyebrow. Those words mean nothing outside their component, which is exactly why they must not sit in `variant` — `variant` is the control emphasis scale, and one prop name answering two questions is how an agent learns the system wrong. This axis is the honest home for a local look, and its values are deliberately not policed.
